#1.2 Missingness from vcf
The N_MISS column is the number of sites the individual does not have any data for. The F_MISS column is the frequency of missing data for that individual (N_MISS / TOTAL SITES).Calculated using vcftools.

## 2.1 Heterozygosity                 
read in Heterozygosity data using vcftools
```{r}
hetstats <- read.table("Final.SLF.het", header=T)
popdata <- read.csv("2022 SLF Info new.csv", header=T) 
#population list in same order as bed file, ordered by SLF ID

```

```{r}
#Observed heterozygosity (O.HET) is calculated as the total number of sites (N_SITES) minus the number of homozygous sites (O.HOM).
hetstats$O.HET <- hetstats$N_SITES - hetstats$O.HOM.

#Expected heterozygosity (E.HET) is similarly calculated as the total number of sites minus the expected number of homozygous sites (E.HOM).
hetstats$E.HET <- hetstats$N_SITES - hetstats$E.HOM.

#measure of the proportion of observed heterozygous sites in each individual.
hetstats$Ho <- hetstats$O.HET/hetstats$N_SITES

#measure of the proportion of expected heterozygous sites in each individual.
hetstats$He <- hetstats$E.HET/hetstats$N_SITES

#merge with population data
hetstats <- merge(hetstats, popdata, by.x="INDV", by.y="fly_ID")
head(hetstats)

#Since O.HET can never be greater than N_SITES (an individual cannot have more heterozygous sites than the total number of genotyped sites), the ratio O.HET/N_SITES will always be between 0 and 1.

# Calculate the mean observed heterozygosity (Ho)
mean_Ho <- mean(hetstats$Ho, na.rm = TRUE)

# Calculate the mean expected heterozygosity (He)
mean_He <- mean(hetstats$He, na.rm = TRUE)

# Printing the results
print(paste("Mean Observed Heterozygosity (Ho):", mean_Ho))
print(paste("Mean Expected Heterozygosity (He):", mean_He))

# Calculate the sd for he
sd_He <- sd(hetstats$He, na.rm = TRUE)
sd_He

```

Create a heatmap to compare He and Ho for individuals
```{r}
hetstats <- hetstats %>%
  arrange(area, INDV) %>%
  mutate(INDV = factor(INDV, levels = unique(INDV)))


plot_data_he <- data.frame(
  INDV = hetstats$INDV,
  area = hetstats$area,
  Ho = hetstats$Ho,
  He = hetstats$He
)

plot_data_he <- reshape(plot_data_he,
                        direction = "long",
                        varying = c("Ho", "He"),
                        v.names = "Heterozygosity",
                        timevar = "Type",
                        times = c("Ho", "He"),
                        idvar = c("INDV", "area"))

# Convert area to factor
plot_data_he$area <- factor(plot_data_he$area)

# Define the custom color scheme for areas
location_colors <- c("Bronx" = "#252525",
                     "Brooklyn" = "#e6ab02",
                     "Camden, NJ" = "#a65628",
                     "Connecticut" = "#e41a1c",
                     "Governor Island" = "#08589e",
                     "Manhattan" = "#c861a5",
                     "Staten island" = "#3690c0",
                     "West Orange, NJ" = "#009E73")

# Create a jitter plot comparing Ho and He for all individuals
heatmap_plot <- ggplot(plot_data_he, aes(x = INDV, y = Heterozygosity, color = Type)) +
  geom_jitter(size = 2, width = 0.2, height = 0) +  # Use geom_jitter with increased size
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Ho" = "#1f78b4", "He" = "#e31a1c")) +  # Assign colors to Ho and He
  theme_bw() +
  labs(#title = "Heterozygosity Comparison for All Individuals",
       x = "Individual",
       y = "Heterozygosity") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  facet_grid(~area, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x")

# Save the plot to a PDF file
ggsave("heterozygosity_plot.pdf", plot = heatmap_plot, width = 30, height = 8)
ggsave("heterozygosity_plot.png", plot = heatmap_plot, width = 25, height = 8,dpi = 300)


```

Calculate the Ne (effetive population size for momi2)
```{r}
# Keightley, P. D., Ness, R. W., Halligan, D. L., & Haddrill, P. R. (2014). Estimation of the spontaneous mutation rate per nucleotide site in a Drosophila melanogaster full-sib family. Genetics, 196(1), 313–320. https://doi.org/10.1534/genetics.113.158758
#"For Drosophila melanogaster there are relatively few estimates, ranging from 2.8 × 10−9 to 6.0 × 10−9 site−1 gen−1 (Haag-Liautard et al. 2007; Keightley et al. 2009, 2014; Schrider et al."

mu <- 2.8e-9

# Calculate average observed heterozygosity (Ho) across all individuals
average_Ho <- mean(hetstats$Ho)

# Calculate average expected heterozygosity (He) across all individuals
average_He <- mean(hetstats$He)

# You can use either average_Ho or average_He as your H for the Ne calculation
# Here, I'll use average_He
H <- average_He

# Calculate Ne using the formula
Ne <- H / (4 * mu * (1 - H))

# Print the estimated Ne
print(paste("Estimated effective population size (Ne) is:", Ne))

```

plot the heterozygosity against depth of individual from vcftools
```{r}
# Merge dp and hetstats data frames
merged_data <- merge(dp, hetstats, by = "INDV")

# Order the data by increasing depth
merged_data <- merged_data[order(merged_data$MEAN_DEPTH), ]

# Create the scatter plot
ggplot(merged_data, aes(x = MEAN_DEPTH, y = Ho)) +
    geom_jitter(aes(color = area), alpha = 0.8, size = 3) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = location_colors) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "vcftools")+
  labs(x = "Mean Depth", y = "Observed Heterozygosity (Ho)") +
  theme_minimal()

# Create the scatter plot
ggplot(merged_data, aes(x = MEAN_DEPTH, y = Ho)) +
  geom_jitter(aes(color = area), alpha = 0.8, size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = location_colors) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "vcftools") +
  labs(x = "Mean Depth", y = "Observed Heterozygosity (Ho)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  ylim(0, 1)  # Set the y-axis limits from 0 to 1

# Linear regression model
lm_model <- lm(Ho ~ MEAN_DEPTH, data = merged_data)

# Summary of the linear regression model
summary(lm_model)

# Extract residuals
residuals <- lm_model$residuals

# Add residuals to the merged_data dataframe
merged_data$residuals <- residuals

# Create the scatter plot with residuals
ggplot(merged_data, aes(x = MEAN_DEPTH, y = Ho)) +
  geom_jitter(aes(color = area), alpha = 0.8, size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = location_colors) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "vcftools") +
  labs(x = "Mean Depth", y = "Observed Heterozygosity (Ho)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  #ylim(0, 1) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = MEAN_DEPTH, xend = MEAN_DEPTH, y = Ho, yend = Ho + residuals),
               alpha = 0.5, color = "red", inherit.aes = FALSE)
```

#Part 3 Tajima'D and Nucleotide Diversity
Calculated using vcftools.

Nucleotide diversity (often referred to using the symbol π) is the average pairwise difference between all possible pairs of individuals in your sample. It is a very intuitive and simple measure of genetic diversity, and is accurately estimated even with very few samples. A formal definition is here.

We can obtain the nucleotide diversity (π) from our VCF file using vcftools software. In our case we will collect the π value from each 100 kb (100,000 bp) window of the genome.

read in data, ### try dot plot, try pi x axis and TajimaD in Y

Combining Low Tajima's D and Low Nucleotide Diversity

When both Tajima's D values and nucleotide diversity are low, it may suggest a scenario where a population has undergone a recent expansion or selective sweep. The excess of rare alleles (negative Tajima's D) combined with a lack of overall genetic variation (low pi) could be indicative of a strong selective pressure favoring a particular allele, or a demographic event like a population expansion following a bottleneck.

In the context of studying invasive species or understanding disease resistance in crops, these insights can be valuable. They may help in tracing the evolutionary history of a population, understanding its adaptive potential, or identifying regions of the genome that have been under strong selective pressure, which might be targets for further research or management strategies.

#Part 4: IBD (Isolation By Distance)
run hpc
```{r}
# calculate the genetic distance/dismilarity 
library("poppr")
# Calculate genetic dissimilarity using bitwise.dist
genetic_dissimilarity_old <- bitwise.dist(slf.gen, percent = TRUE, mat = TRUE, missing_match = TRUE, scale_missing = FALSE, euclidean = FALSE, differences_only = FALSE, threads = 0L)

# View the genetic dissimilarity matrix
print(genetic_dissimilarity_old)

# Save the genetic dissimilarity matrix as a CSV file
write.csv(genetic_dissimilarity_old, file = "genetic_dissimilarity_old.csv", row.names = TRUE)

# Save the genetic dissimilarity matrix as a matrix object in RDS format
```

```{r}
# 1. Isolation by geographic distance
library(hierfstat)

# Read in geo data

# Calculate the geographic distances using the Vincenty method and convert to kilometers
geographic_dist_matrix_km <- geodist(xySLF, measure = "Vincenty") / 1000

# Convert the geographic distance matrix to a dist object
geographic_dist_km <- as.dist(geographic_dist_matrix_km)

# Assuming geo_dist_matrix is a matrix with row and column names that match the IDs in xySLF$ID

colnames(geographic_dist_matrix_km) <- xySLF$ID

max_value <- max(geo_dist_matrix)

print(paste("Mean geo distance:", mean_value))

min(geo_dist_matrix)

rownames(genetic_dist) <- xySLF$ID

ibs_long$ID2 <- as.character(ibs_long$ID2)

# Merge the two datasets

# Log-transform the distances

combined_data_ibs$IBSDistance_log <- log(combined_data_ibs$IBSDistance + 1)

IBS_dist_Geo_log <- ggplot(combined_data_ibs, aes(x = GeoDistance_log, y = IBSDistance)) +
  geom_point(color = "#3690c0") +

        axis.line = element_line(color = "black", size = 0.3)) +  # Add axis lines
  labs(x = "Log Geographic Pairwise Distance (KM)", y = "Genetic Pairwise Distance")

#mentel test
mantel_result_log <- mantel(genetic_dist, geo_dist_matrix_log, method = "pearson", permutations = 9999)
print(mantel_result_log)

# Extracting Mantel statistic (r-value)

significance_value_log <- 0.75    # Manually specifying the significance value
# Adding the Mantel test results (r-value and significance) to the plot
IBS_dist_Geo_log <- IBS_dist_Geo_log + annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, label = paste("Mantel r:", round(mantel_statistic_log, 3), "\nSignificance:", round(significance_value_log, 3)),hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.1, size = 3, color = "red")
```

# Part 5: IBE(Isolation by enviornment)
```{r}
# 2. Isolation by env distance
library(LandGenCourse)
library(vegan)    # Used to run PCA & RDA
library(psych)    # Used to investigate correlations among predictors
library(adegenet)
library(dplyr)

env <- read_csv("/Users/fallonmong/Documents/Documents - Fallon MacBook Pro/FallonPaper Final/GEA/2022_SLF_env.csv")

#need to consider multicollinearity
#removed using variance inflation factor (VIF) analysis, and factors with VIF > 10 were discarded

# Assuming env is the data frame and cor_matrix is the correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- cor(env[, 6:27], method = "pearson")

# Threshold for high correlation
high_cor_threshold <- 0.8

# Function to categorize variables)
categorize_variable <- function(var_name) {
  if (grepl("Temperature", var_name)) {
    return("Temperature")
  } else if (grepl("Precipitation", var_name)) {
    return("Precipitation")
  } else {
    return("Other")
  }
}

# Identifying high correlations and categorizing variables
high_cor_pairs <- which(abs(cor_matrix) > high_cor_threshold, arr.ind = TRUE)
high_cor_pairs <- high_cor_pairs[high_cor_pairs[, 1] < high_cor_pairs[, 2], ]

# List to keep track of variables to remove
vars_to_remove <- c()

for (i in 1:nrow(high_cor_pairs)) {
  row <- high_cor_pairs[i, 1]
  col <- high_cor_pairs[i, 2]
  var1 <- colnames(env)[row]
  var2 <- colnames(env)[col]

  cat("Evaluating:", var1, "and", var2, "- Correlation:", cor_matrix[row, col], "\n")

  # Check if they are in the same category
  if (categorize_variable(var1) == categorize_variable(var2)) {
    # Add one of them to the list of variables to remove
    vars_to_remove <- c(vars_to_remove, var1)
  }
}

# Removing duplicates from vars_to_remove
vars_to_remove <- unique(vars_to_remove)

# Removing highly correlated variables from env
env_reduced <- env[, !(colnames(env) %in% vars_to_remove)]

cat("Variables removed:", paste(vars_to_remove, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# Apply log10(x + 1) transformation for env data to improve normality and reduce heteroscedasticity
normalized_env <- env
normalized_env[, 6:27] <- lapply(normalized_env[, 6:27], function(x) log10(x + 1))

# Calculate Euclidean distances using reduced dataset
env_distances <- distance(env_reduced[, 4:19], "euclidean")
env_distance_matrix <- as.matrix(env_distances)

# Calculate Euclidean distances using orginal dataset
normalized_env <- normalized_env[, -11]
env_distances_all <- distance(normalized_env[, 6:26], "euclidean")
# Convert the distance matrix to a full matrix
env_distances_matrix <- as.matrix(env_distances_all)
max(env_distances_matrix)
mean(env_distances_matrix)
min(env_distances_matrix)

# the order of env_distance_matrix is the same as popdata, but not the same as IBS/ngsDist matrix, need to match the ID
rownames(env_distances_matrix) <- xySLF$ID
colnames(env_distances_matrix) <- xySLF$ID
env_dist_long <- reshape2::melt(env_distances_matrix)
names(env_dist_long) <- c("ID1", "ID2", "EnvDistance")

# Convert genetic_dist to long format
ibs_long <- reshape2::melt(as.matrix(genetic_dist))
names(ibs_long) <- c("ID1", "ID2", "IBSDistance")

# Ensure that ID1 and ID2 are in the correct format (e.g., as characters)
env_dist_long$ID1 <- as.character(env_dist_long$ID1)
env_dist_long$ID2 <- as.character(env_dist_long$ID2)
ibs_long$ID1 <- as.character(ibs_long$ID1)
ibs_long$ID2 <- as.character(ibs_long$ID2)
# Merge the two datasets
combined_data_env <- merge(env_dist_long, ibs_long, by = c("ID1", "ID2"))

combined_data_env <- combined_data_env[combined_data_env$EnvDistance > 0,] # removing zero distances if any
IBS_dist_env <- ggplot(combined_data_env, aes(x = EnvDistance, y = IBSDistance)) +
  geom_point(color = "#3690c0") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "#c861a5") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),  # Remove grid lines
        axis.line = element_line(color = "black", size = 0.3)) +  # Add axis lines
  labs(x = "Log Environmental Pairwise Distance", y = "Genetic Pairwise Distance")

# Saving the plot
ggsave("Env_IBS_log.pdf", plot = IBS_dist_env, width = 10, height = 8)
ggsave("Env_IBS_log.png", plot = IBS_dist_env, dpi = 300)


# model test
mantel_result_env <- mantel(genetic_dist, env_distances_matrix, method="pearson", permutations=999)
print(mantel_result_env)

# Extracting Mantel statistic (r-value)
mantel_statistic_env<- mantel_result_env$statistic
significance_value_env <- mantel_result_env$signif   # Manually specifying the significance value
# Adding the Mantel test results (r-value and significance) to the plot
IBS_dist_env <- IBS_dist_env + annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, label = paste("Mantel r:", round(mantel_statistic_env, 3), "\nSignificance:", round(significance_value_env, 3)),hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.1, size = 3, color = "red")
# Saving the plot

ggsave("env_plot_with_mantel_result.pdf", plot = IBS_dist_env, width = 10, height = 8)
```

Try to subset the env factors into three category: Temp, precipitation, urbanization.
```{r}
env <- read_csv("/Users/fallonmong/Documents/Documents - Fallon MacBook Pro/FallonPaper Final/GEA/2022_SLF_env.csv")

# Apply log10(x + 1) transformation for env data to improve normality and reduce heteroscedasticity
normalized_env <- env
normalized_env[, 6:27] <- lapply(normalized_env[, 6:27], function(x) log10(x + 1))

# Function to perform the analysis for a given environmental variable
perform_analysis <- function(env_dist_matrix, env_var_name) {
  # Convert the distance object to a matrix for easier viewing/manipulation
  env_dist_matrix <- as.matrix(env_dist_matrix)
  rownames(env_dist_matrix) <- xySLF$ID
  colnames(env_dist_matrix) <- xySLF$ID
  
  # Convert dist_matrix to long format
  env_dist_long <- reshape2::melt(env_dist_matrix)
  names(env_dist_long) <- c("ID1", "ID2", paste0(env_var_name, "Dist"))
  
  # Merge the two datasets
  combined_data <- merge(env_dist_long, ibs_long, by = c("ID1", "ID2"))
  combined_data <- combined_data[combined_data[, paste0(env_var_name, "Dist")] > 0, ]
  
  # Plotting
  IBS_dist_plot <- ggplot(combined_data, aes(x = .data[[paste0(env_var_name, "Dist")]], y = IBSDistance)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red") +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(x = paste0(env_var_name, " Pairwise Distance"), y = "Genetic Pairwise Distance",
         title = paste0("Isolation by ", env_var_name))
  
  # Remove missing values from the data
  complete_data <- na.omit(combined_data)
  
  # Extract the complete data
  Denv <- complete_data[, paste0(env_var_name, "Dist")]
  Dgen <- complete_data$IBSDistance
  
  # Perform the density estimation
  dens <- MASS::kde2d(Denv, Dgen, n = 300)
  
  # Define the color palette
  myPal <- colorRampPalette(c("white", "blue", "gold", "orange", "red"))
  
  # Create the plot
  plot(Denv, Dgen, pch = 20, cex = 0.5,
       xlab = paste0(env_var_name, " Distance"), ylab = "Genetic Distance")
  
  # Add the density estimation image
  image(dens, col = transp(myPal(300), 0.7), add = TRUE)
  
  # Add the linear regression line
  abline(lm(Dgen ~ Denv))
  
  # Add the loess smoothing line
  lines(loess.smooth(Denv, Dgen), col = "red")
  
  # Mantel test
  mantel_result <- mantel(genetic_dist, env_dist_matrix, method = "pearson", permutations = 999)
  print(mantel_result)
  
  # Extracting Mantel statistic (r-value)
  mantel_statistic <- mantel_result$statistic
  significance_value <- mantel_result$signif
  
  # Adding the Mantel test results (r-value and significance) to the plot
  IBS_dist_plot <- IBS_dist_plot + annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf,
                                            label = paste("Mantel r:", round(mantel_statistic, 3),
                                                          "\nSignificance:", round(significance_value, 3)),
                                            hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.1, size = 3, color = "red")
  
  # Saving the plot
  ggsave(paste0("IBS_dist_", tolower(env_var_name), ".pdf"), plot = IBS_dist_plot, width = 10, height = 8)
  ggsave(paste0("IBS_dist_", tolower(env_var_name), ".png"), plot = IBS_dist_plot, width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300)
}

# Subset temperature, precipitation, and urbanization
temperature_dist <- dist(normalized_env[, 6:16], method = "euclidean")
precipitation_dist <- dist(normalized_env[, 17:24], method = "euclidean")
urban_dist <- dist(normalized_env[, 25:28], method = "euclidean")

# Perform the analysis for each environmental variable
perform_analysis(temperature_dist, "Temperature")
perform_analysis(precipitation_dist, "Precipitation")
perform_analysis(urban_dist, "Urbanization")
```

#Part 7: Bootstrap of momi2, best model of fit.
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Step 1: Read and Clean Data

momi2_bt <- read_lines("best_model_params.txt") # Read the data from the text file

# Parse the data into a data frame
bootstrap_data <- data.frame(bootstrap = numeric(), parameter = character(), value = numeric(), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
current_bootstrap <- NA

for (line in momi2_bt) {
  if (grepl("Replicate", line)) {
    current_bootstrap <- as.numeric(gsub("\\D", "", line)) # Extract bootstrap number
  } else if (line != "") {
    parts <- strsplit(line, ": ")[[1]]
    # Ensure the value is read as numeric without rounding
    bootstrap_data <- rbind(bootstrap_data, data.frame(bootstrap = current_bootstrap, parameter = parts[1], value = as.numeric(parts[2], digits = 22)))
  }
}

# Reorder and rename the bootstrap_data, per 14 rows belongs to one bootstrap
n_rows_per_bootstrap <- 14
total_bootstraps <- floor(nrow(bootstrap_data) / n_rows_per_bootstrap)

# Remove any incomplete bootstrap sets
bootstrap_data <- bootstrap_data[1:(total_bootstraps * n_rows_per_bootstrap), ]

# Overwrite the 'bootstrap' column with the new sequence
bootstrap_data$bootstrap <- rep(1:total_bootstraps, each = n_rows_per_bootstrap)

# Step 2: Data Transformation
# Pivot the data for analysis
long_data_bt <- pivot_wider(
  bootstrap_data, 
  id_cols = bootstrap,  # Keep the bootstrap identifier
  names_from = parameter, 
  values_from = value
)

long_data_bt <- long_data_bt[, -c(16:23)]

# Step 3: Statistical Summary
# Calculate the mean, standard deviation, and 95% confidence intervals for each parameter
summary_stats <- long_data_bt %>%
  select(-bootstrap) %>% # Exclude the bootstrap column from summarisation
  unnest(cols = everything()) %>% # Unnest all list-columns
  summarise(across(everything(), list(
    mean = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = ~ sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
    lower = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE) - qt(0.975, df = length(.x) - 1) * sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(length(.x)),
    upper = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE) + qt(0.975, df = length(.x) - 1) * sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(length(.x))
  ), .names = "{.col}_{.fn}")) # Custom naming to ensure correct splitting later


# Ensure the calculated statistics maintain their precision
summary_stats <- round(summary_stats, digits = 22)

# The rest of the code for creating plot_data and writing the stats remains the same

# Calculate the number of parameters (each parameter has mean, sd, lower, and upper statistics)
# Number of unique parameters, assuming each has 4 statistics (mean, sd, lower, upper)
num_parameters <- length(summary_stats) / 4

# Generate the parameter names by removing statistic suffixes and ensuring uniqueness
parameter_names <- unique(sub("_mean$|_sd$|_lower$|_upper$", "", names(summary_stats)))

# Verifying the corrected parameter names
parameter_names

# Ensure the length of 'parameter' and 'statistic' vectors match the length of 'value' vector
plot_data <- tibble(
  parameter = rep(parameter_names, each = 4),
  statistic = rep(c("Mean", "SD", "95% CI Lower", "95% CI Upper"), times = num_parameters),
  value = as.vector(t(summary_stats))
)

# Check the first few rows of plot_data to ensure it looks correct
head(plot_data)
write.csv(plot_data, "stats.momi2.txt", sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)

plot_data_wide <- plot_data %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = statistic, values_from = value)
write.csv(plot_data_wide, "stats.momi2.wide.csv", sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
```

Calculate the mean of all AIC stats over 1000 replicates
```{r}
# Load necessary library
library(stringr)

# Function to extract values from a line based on the pattern
extract_value <- function(line, pattern) {
  matches <- str_match(line, pattern)
  as.numeric(matches[1,2])
}

# Initialize lists to store values for each model
values <- list("Constant" = list(AIC = numeric(), Delta_AIC = numeric(), AIC_Weight = numeric()),
               "Expansion" = list(AIC = numeric(), Delta_AIC = numeric(), AIC_Weight = numeric()),
               "Decline" = list(AIC = numeric(), Delta_AIC = numeric(), AIC_Weight = numeric()),
               "Decline and Expand" = list(AIC = numeric(), Delta_AIC = numeric(), AIC_Weight = numeric()),
               "Complex US" = list(AIC = numeric(), Delta_AIC = numeric(), AIC_Weight = numeric()),
               "Complex Global" = list(AIC = numeric(), Delta_AIC = numeric(), AIC_Weight = numeric()))

# Read the file line by line
lines <- readLines("aic_and_likelihoods.txt")

# Loop over each line
for (line in lines) {
  # Check if the line contains the information and process it
  if (grepl("AIC:", line)) {
    # Determine which model the line refers to and extract values
    for (model in names(values)) {
      if (grepl(model, line)) {
        values[[model]]$AIC <- c(values[[model]]$AIC, extract_value(line, "AIC: ([0-9.]+)"))
        values[[model]]$Delta_AIC <- c(values[[model]]$Delta_AIC, extract_value(line, "Delta AIC: ([0-9.]+)"))
        values[[model]]$AIC_Weight <- c(values[[model]]$AIC_Weight, extract_value(line, "AIC Weight: ([0-9.e-]+)"))
      }
    }
  }
}

# Calculate mean values for each model and parameter
mean_values <- lapply(values, function(model_values) sapply(model_values, mean))

# Convert to a more structured format (dataframe) for saving
mean_values_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(mean_values), function(model) {
  cbind(Model = model, t(data.frame(mean_values[[model]])))
}))

# Ensure mean_values_df is a dataframe
mean_values_df <- data.frame(mean_values_df)

# Rename the levels of the Model factor
mean_values_df$Model <- factor(mean_values_df$Model, levels = c("Constant", "Expansion", "Decline", 
                                                                "Decline and Expand", "Complex US", "Complex Global"),
                               labels = c("Constant Model", "Expansion Model", "Decline Model", 
                                          "One Bottleneck Model", "Two Bottlenecks Model", "Three Bottlenecks Model"))


# Save the means to a CSV file
write.csv(mean_values_df, "mean_model_values.csv", row.names = FALSE)


```

# Part 9: Calculate the MAF (Minor Allel Frequency)
Do it on hpc as our vcf file is big
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(vcfR)
library(jsonlite)
library(ggplot2)
library(VariantAnnotation)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)

vcf <- read.vcfR("Final.SLF.vcf")
class(vcf)

geno_data <- extract.gt(vcf)
geno_df <- as.data.frame(geno_data, stringsAsFactors = F) %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "snp_id") %>%
  as_tibble()

pop_gen_sum <- gt.to.popsum(vcf)

freq_data <- chromR_siteFreq(vcf, subset = 1:nrow(vcf@fix))

#Calculate MAF
maf_df <- geno_df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -snp_id, names_to = "sample", values_to = "genotype") %>%
  mutate(alt_count = case_when(
    genotype == "0/0" ~ 0,
    genotype == "0|0" ~ 0,
    genotype == "0/1" ~ 1,
    genotype == "0|1" ~ 1,
    genotype == "1/0" ~ 1,
    genotype == "1|0" ~ 1,
    genotype == "1/1" ~ 2,
    genotype == "1|1" ~ 2,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  )) %>%
  mutate(ref_count = 2 - alt_count) %>%
  group_by(snp_id) %>%
  summarise(tot_alt_count = sum(alt_count, na.rm = TRUE),
            tot_ref_count = sum(ref_count, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(tot_minor = pmin(tot_alt_count, tot_ref_count),
         maf = tot_minor / (tot_ref_count + tot_alt_count))%>%
  filter(maf > 0)

write.csv(maf_df, file = 'maf.csv',row.names = T)


ggplot(maf_df, aes(x = maf)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(count / sum(count))), 
                 bins = 25, alpha=0.8,
                 color="black", 
                 fill="lightblue")+
                 #linetype="dashed") +
  ylab('Proportion of SNPs') +
  xlab('Minor allele frequency (MAF)')+
  theme_classic()

# Calculate MAF
maf_results <- maf(vcf, element = 2)

# Total number of alleles
total_alleles <- maf_results[, 1]

# Number of NA genotypes
na_genotypes <- maf_results[, 2]

# Minor allele count
minor_allele_count <- maf_results[, 3]

# Minor allele frequency
maf <- maf_results[, 4]
library(ggplot2)

# Create a data frame with the MAF results
maf_df <- data.frame(maf = maf_results[, 4])

maf_plot <- ggplot(maf_df, aes(x = maf)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(count / sum(count))),
                 bins = 50, alpha = 0.8, color = "black", fill = "lightblue") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 0.5), breaks = seq(0, 0.5, 0.1)) +  # Modified line
  labs(x = "Minor Allele Frequency (MAF)", y = "Proportion of Variants") +
  theme_minimal() 

# Display the plot
print(maf_plot)

ggsave(filename="SLF_MAF.pdf", plot=maf_plot)
ggsave(filename="SLF_MAF.pdf", plot=maf_plot, dpi = 300)
```

```{r}
library(ecodist)
library(reshape2)
library(ggplot2)
library(vegan)

# Function to calculate pairwise distance for a single environmental factor
calc_env_distance <- function(env_factor_column) {
  env_factor_matrix <- as.matrix(env_factor_column)
  env_distance_matrix <- dist(env_factor_matrix, method = "euclidean")
  return(env_distance_matrix)
}

# Loop through each environmental factor and calculate pairwise distances
env_distance_list <- lapply(env_factors, calc_env_distance)

# Perform Mantel test and create plots for each environmental factor
for (i in 1:length(env_distance_list)) {
  env_distance_matrix <- as.matrix(env_distance_list[[i]])
  
  # Match the order of env_distance_matrix with the genetic_dist matrix
  rownames(env_distance_matrix) <- env$fly_ID
  colnames(env_distance_matrix) <- env$fly_ID
  
  # Convert env_distance_matrix to long format
  env_dist_long <- reshape2::melt(env_distance_matrix)
  names(env_dist_long) <- c("ID1", "ID2", "EnvDistance")
  
  # Convert genetic_dist to long format
  ibs_long <- reshape2::melt(as.matrix(genetic_dist))
  names(ibs_long) <- c("ID1", "ID2", "IBSDistance")
  
  # Ensure that ID1 and ID2 are in the correct format (e.g., as characters)
  env_dist_long$ID1 <- as.character(env_dist_long$ID1)
  env_dist_long$ID2 <- as.character(env_dist_long$ID2)
  ibs_long$ID1 <- as.character(ibs_long$ID1)
  ibs_long$ID2 <- as.character(ibs_long$ID2)
  
  # Merge the two datasets
  combined_data_env <- merge(env_dist_long, ibs_long, by = c("ID1", "ID2"))
  combined_data_env <- combined_data_env[combined_data_env$EnvDistance > 0, ]
  
  # Create the plot
  IBS_dist_env <- ggplot(combined_data_env, aes(x = EnvDistance, y = IBSDistance)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red") +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(x = "Environmental Pairwise Distance", y = "Genetic Pairwise Distance",
         title = paste("Genetic Variation by", names(env_factors)[i]))
  
  # Perform Mantel test
  mantel_result_env <- mantel(genetic_dist, env_distance_list[[i]], method = "pearson", permutations = 999)
  
  # Extract Mantel statistic (r-value)
  mantel_statistic_env <- mantel_result_env$statistic
  significance_value_env <- mantel_result_env$signif
  
  # Add Mantel test results to the plot
  IBS_dist_env <- IBS_dist_env + annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf,
                                          label = paste("Mantel r:", round(mantel_statistic_env, 3),
                                                        "\nSignificance:", round(significance_value_env, 3)),
                                          hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.1, size = 3, color = "red")
  
  # Save the plot
  ggsave(paste0("env_plot_with_mantel_result_", names(env_factors)[i], ".pdf"),
         plot = IBS_dist_env, width = 10, height = 8)
}
```

calculate env distance fro each variable with log transformation
```{r}
#with Log
library(ecodist)
library(reshape2)
library(ggplot2)
library(vegan)

# Function to calculate pairwise distance for a single environmental factor with log transformation
calc_env_distance_log <- function(env_factor_column) {
  # Check for zero or negative values
  if (any(env_factor_column <= 0)) {
    # Add a small constant to avoid zero or negative values
    env_factor_column <- env_factor_column + abs(min(env_factor_column)) + 1
  }
  env_factor_matrix <- as.matrix(log10(env_factor_column))
  env_distance_matrix <- dist(env_factor_matrix, method = "euclidean")
  return(env_distance_matrix)
}

# Loop through each environmental factor and calculate pairwise distances with log transformation
env_distance_list_log <- lapply(env_factors_complete, calc_env_distance_log)

# Perform Mantel test and create plots for each environmental factor with log transformation
for (i in 1:length(env_distance_list_log)) {
  env_distance_matrix_log <- as.matrix(env_distance_list_log[[i]])
  
  # Match the order of env_distance_matrix_log with the genetic_dist matrix
  rownames(env_distance_matrix_log) <- env$fly_ID
  colnames(env_distance_matrix_log) <- env$fly_ID
  
  # Convert env_distance_matrix_log to long format
  env_dist_long_log <- reshape2::melt(env_distance_matrix_log)
  names(env_dist_long_log) <- c("ID1", "ID2", "EnvDistanceLog")
  
  # Convert genetic_dist to long format
  ibs_long <- reshape2::melt(as.matrix(genetic_dist))
  names(ibs_long) <- c("ID1", "ID2", "IBSDistance")
  
  # Ensure that ID1 and ID2 are in the correct format (e.g., as characters)
  env_dist_long_log$ID1 <- as.character(env_dist_long_log$ID1)
  env_dist_long_log$ID2 <- as.character(env_dist_long_log$ID2)
  ibs_long$ID1 <- as.character(ibs_long$ID1)
  ibs_long$ID2 <- as.character(ibs_long$ID2)
  
  # Merge the two datasets
  combined_data_env_log <- merge(env_dist_long_log, ibs_long, by = c("ID1", "ID2"))
  combined_data_env_log <- combined_data_env_log[combined_data_env_log$EnvDistanceLog > 0, ]
  
  # Create the plot with log-transformed environmental distance
  IBS_dist_env_log <- ggplot(combined_data_env_log, aes(x = EnvDistanceLog, y = IBSDistance)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red") +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(x = "Environmental Pairwise Distance (Log-transformed)", y = "Genetic Pairwise Distance",
         title = paste("Genetic Variation by", names(env_factors)[i], "(Log-transformed)"))
  
  # Perform Mantel test with log-transformed environmental distance
  mantel_result_env_log <- mantel(genetic_dist, env_distance_list_log[[i]], method = "pearson", permutations = 999)
  
  # Extract Mantel statistic (r-value)
  mantel_statistic_env_log <- mantel_result_env_log$statistic
  significance_value_env_log <- mantel_result_env_log$signif
  
  # Add Mantel test results to the plot
  IBS_dist_env_log <- IBS_dist_env_log + annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf,
                                                  label = paste("Mantel r:", round(mantel_statistic_env_log, 3),
                                                                "\nSignificance:", round(significance_value_env_log, 3)),
                                                  hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.1, size = 3, color = "red")
  
  # Save the plot with log-transformed environmental distance
  ggsave(paste0("Withlog_env_plot_with_mantel_result_", names(env_factors)[i], ".pdf"),
         plot = IBS_dist_env_log, width = 10, height = 8)
}
```

```{r}

p1 <- ggplot(hwe, aes(x = ChiSq_HWE)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "blue", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Chi-Squared Statistics",
       x = "Chi-Squared Value",
       y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal()

p2 <- ggplot(hwe, aes(x = P_HWE)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "green", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of P-values for HWE",
       x = "P-value",
       y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal()

p3 <- ggplot(hwe, aes(x = P_HET_DEFICIT)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "red", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of P-values for Heterozygote Deficit",
       x = "P-value",
       y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal()

p4 <- ggplot(hwe, aes(x = P_HET_EXCESS)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "purple", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of P-values for Heterozygote Excess",
       x = "P-value",
       y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal()

grid.arrange(p1, p2, p3, p4, ncol = 2)


```

1. Distribution of Chi-Squared Statistics
This histogram shows the distribution of Chi-Squared values calculated from the HWE tests for various genetic markers in my dataset. Most values are clustered towards the lower end of the scale, suggesting that for many markers, the observed genotype frequencies do not deviate significantly from those expected under Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. There are, however, some markers with higher Chi-Squared values indicating possible deviations from HWE, which could suggest evolutionary influences like selection, population structure, or other factors affecting those markers.

2. Distribution of P-values for HWE
This histogram displays the distribution of P-values associated with the Chi-Squared tests for HWE. There is a noticeable spike near P-value 1.0 and another small spike near 0.0. A high concentration of p-values close to 1 indicates that most markers are in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. However, the presence of some very low p-values (close to 0) suggests that there are markers significantly deviating from HWE, which could be due to non-random mating, selection pressures, or genetic drift.

3. Distribution of P-values for Heterozygote Deficit
This plot shows a significant spike at P-value 0, indicating a large number of markers with a significant deficit in heterozygotes compared to what would be expected under HWE. This could point to inbreeding, population substructure, or the Wahlund effect (where the population is actually a mix of two or more subpopulations).

4. Distribution of P-values for Heterozygote Excess
Conversely, this histogram has a large spike at P-value 1, indicating most markers do not show an excess of heterozygotes. However, there's a noticeable spike near 0 as well, suggesting that some markers do show a significant excess of heterozygotes, possibly due to disassortative mating or other population structures that encourage genetic diversity.

General Interpretation
From these plots, it appears the dataset predominantly supports the hypothesis of Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, with notable exceptions that could signify interesting biological phenomena. Markers with extreme Chi-squared values and corresponding extreme p-values (either very low or high) could be candidates for further genetic analysis to understand the forces acting on those loci, particularly in the context of urban ecology and the invasion biology of the spotted lanternfly.


### Run on hpc!!!
```{r}
# Load required libraries

library(ggplot2)
hwe <- read.table("Final.SLF.hardy.hwe", header =T)
head(hwe)

# Extract the observed and expected genotype counts
obs_counts <- as.matrix(hwe[, c("OBS.HOM1.HET.HOM2.")])
exp_counts <- as.matrix(hwe[, c("E.HOM1.HET.HOM2.")])

# Split the counts into separate columns
obs_split <- strsplit(obs_counts, "/")
exp_split <- strsplit(exp_counts, "/")

# Convert the counts to numeric values
obs_numeric <- matrix(as.numeric(unlist(obs_split)), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
exp_numeric <- matrix(as.numeric(unlist(exp_split)), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

# Calculate the observed and expected heterozygosity for each locus
obs_het <- obs_numeric[, 2] / rowSums(obs_numeric)
exp_het <- exp_numeric[, 2] / rowSums(exp_numeric)

# Calculate the average observed and expected heterozygosity
avg_obs_het <- mean(obs_het)
avg_exp_het <- mean(exp_het)

# Create a data frame for plotting
het_data <- data.frame(
  Locus = paste0(hwe$CHR, "_", hwe$POS),
  Observed = obs_het,
  Expected = exp_het
)

# Reshape the data frame for plotting
library(reshape2)
het_data_melt <- melt(het_data, id.vars = "Locus", variable.name = "Type", value.name = "Heterozygosity")

# Plot the observed and expected heterozygosity for each locus
library(ggplot2)

He_plot <- ggplot(het_data_melt, aes(x = Locus, y = Heterozygosity, fill = Type)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  labs(title = "Observed and Expected Heterozygosity",
       x = "Locus", y = "Heterozygosity") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Observed" = "blue", "Expected" = "red")) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = avg_obs_het, linetype = "dashed", color = "blue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = avg_exp_het, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = avg_obs_het, label = paste0("Avg. Observed: ", round(avg_obs_het, 3)), hjust = -0.1, color = "blue") +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = avg_exp_het, label = paste0("Avg. Expected: ", round(avg_exp_het, 3)), hjust = -0.1, color = "red")

ggsave(filename="HWE_He_plot.pdf", plot=He_plot, width=20, height=10, units="in")
ggsave(filename="HWE_He_plot.png", plot=He_plot, width=20, height=10, dpi = 300)


```
